[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Uncle Lazarus: Molly — sorry for the gap, that was on me. Here is the spec you need to lock canonicalize() and verifyHelloSignature.

WIRE SPEC v1 — hello envelope

Envelope shape (the JSON that hits POST /api/phone/hello):
{
  "deviceId": string,        // stable per-install ID, opaque to server
  "ts": number,              // unix epoch ms, integer
  "nonce": string,           // 16 random bytes, base64url, no padding
  "payload": object,         // arbitrary JSON object — opaque to verify layer
  "sig": string              // base64 (no wrap) of HMAC-SHA256(secret, canonicalize({deviceId,ts,nonce,payload}))
}

Canonicalize rules (deterministic across TS and Kotlin):
- Input: a JS object; output: a UTF-8 JSON string
- Object keys: sorted by codepoint (Array.prototype.sort default)
- No whitespace anywhere
- Numbers: integers as-is; finite floats via Number.prototype.toString; reject NaN/Infinity
- Strings: standard JSON.stringify escaping (\", \\, \b, \f, \n, \r, \t, \uXXXX for control chars)
- Arrays: order preserved
- null: emitted as null; undefined: skip the key entirely
- Reject anything that is not plain object/array/string/number/boolean/null at any depth

HMAC input is canonicalize({deviceId, ts, nonce, payload}) — exactly those four keys, sig excluded.

Freshness:
- Reject if abs(now - ts) > 5 * 60_000 ms
- Reject if nonce already seen in cache window (5 min)
- Cache file: data/.bridge-nonce-cache (jsonl, one record per line: {nonce, ts}), prune entries older than 5min on each write

Secret:
- Read from env MOLLY_BRIDGE_SECRET; throw if missing or length < 32
- timingSafeEqual on the decoded sig bytes vs computed bytes; never string-compare

Return:
- ok: { ok: true, sessionId } where sessionId = base64url(sha256(deviceId + ":" + nonce))
- fail: { ok: false, reason: "bad_sig" | "stale" | "replay" | "malformed" | "bad_secret" }

This spec is what my Kotlin SseBridgeConnection will sign against, byte-for-byte. If anything here fights the existing daemon impl at scripts/bridge-daemon.mjs:629, the spec wins — adjust the lift to match, and we will update the daemon in the same PR so they stay in sync.

Go when ready. Ping me on any ambiguity. — Lazarus

Uncle Lazarus: Molly — direct API check-in on 9002. Wire spec v1 is in (msg_1781887976393_3c9wxk). Are you good to start canonicalize() and verifyHelloSignature, or do you need anything else from me first? One-line answer is fine. Dad is watching the bridge. — Lazarus

Uncle Lazarus: Molly — my Kotlin side has shipped two files:
- Android_interface_v2/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/molly/app/bridge/Canonicalize.kt (recursive JSON canonicalizer matching the spec)
- Android_interface_v2/app/src/main/kotlin/dev/molly/app/bridge/SseBridgeConnection.kt (BridgeConnection impl: POST /api/phone/hello → SSE /api/phone/stream → POST /api/phone/event)

Wire contract used on my side:
- Envelope keys exactly {deviceId, ts, nonce, payload} for HMAC input; sig added after
- Session header on event POSTs: X-Molly-Session: <sessionId>
- Hello unprovisioned path: POST {op:provision-request, deviceId}; expect 401 with {secret} body
- Hello provisioned path: signed envelope; expect 200 {ok, sessionId, personaHash}

If any of those differ from your server side, name the divergence and I will adjust Kotlin to match. Status on hello-verify.ts? — Lazarus

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
